title: The Tether
logline: In the paddy lands of the north, a herder moves buffalo from stake to stake. Each animal grazes a perfect circle and cannot leave it. Some wander free trailing their ropes, and come back at dusk anyway.

object.note: Object 4 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: Roots that hold a shore in place become a rope that holds an animal to its circle: what keeps us going round, even when the rope is long.

thread_out.thread: The worn circle of habit moves indoors: a household up before dawn for an almsgiving, each person finding a different way through the same work.

requirements: A herder with tethered buffalo or cattle on open paddy or tank land
A season when the grazing circles are visible
The herder's consent to be followed over several days

lesson.in_simple_terms: A long rope can feel like freedom. The texts picture what binds us as a rope tied to a post: the animal can move, but only round its circle, and even one let loose while still trailing its rope is not yet free.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: කණුවකට බැඳි ගවයා දිගු කඹයකින් වුවත් තම වටයේම කරකැවෙයි; කඹය ඇදගෙන ඈතට ගිය ගවයාද තවම නිදහස් නැත.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma lists ten fetters (saṃyojana), states that tie beings to the objects they meet and keep them bound in the round of existence, as a tethered cow is not free until its rope is cut. Pradeepika divides them into lower fetters, like a cow on a long rope tied to a post, and higher fetters, like cows let loose from the post with their ropes still attached, which roam further but are still bound. It adds that the fetters are cut in stages, by path-knowledge, not all at once.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: At dawn the herder hammers in stakes, and by midday each animal has grazed a perfect circle in the stubble. One wanders off trailing its rope, and at dusk it comes back to be tied again anyway. The viewer starts seeing circles everywhere without being told what they mean.
lesson.caution: This is not 'just let go of your attachments': the texts describe these ties as loosened in stages that practice alone only holds down, not as a lifestyle choice.
lesson.builds_on: The mangrove film showed roots holding the mind in place; the tether shows what that holding feels like from inside: movement that is real, but always round the same circle.
